couplets.gloss: Her eyes have two kinds of look: one hurts you, and the other is the only cure for that hurt.
keywords: the way she looks at me

edges.reason: Her eyes act on him twice over, bringing sickness with one look and curing it with the other.
edges.quote: Her kohl-lined eyes hold two looks

edges.reason: The second look is medicine for the very sickness the first one gave him.
edges.quote: the other is the medicine for it

couplets.gloss: A quick secret look thrown your way when you aren't watching is worth more than half of everything love has to give.

edges.reason: Rates one stolen glance at more than half of desire.
edges.quote: That small glance her eyes steal at me

couplets.gloss: She glanced at me, then lowered her head, and that small gesture was what made our new love grow.

edges.reason: A look and a bowed head are credited with feeding the bond between them.
edges.quote: having looked she bowed her head

edges.reason: Her look and her bowed head are water poured on their bond, as on a growing plant.
edges.quote: water she poured on the bond between us

couplets.gloss: She looks down whenever I look at her, but the moment I turn away she watches me and smiles to herself.

edges.reason: Gives the classic pattern: eyes on the ground while watched, on him once he turns away.
edges.quote: When I look at her, she looks at the ground

edges.reason: Shows someone newly in love what to watch for: the look that comes only when yours turns away.
edges.quote: When I don’t, she looks at me and softly smiles

couplets.gloss: She doesn't look straight at me, but she half-closes one eye as if by chance and smiles at me all the same.

edges.reason: A smile with one eye narrowed says what her averted eyes will not.
edges.quote: As if narrowing one eye, she smiles

couplets.gloss: Even when people in love talk as if they barely know each other, anyone can tell at once what their words really mean.

edges.reason: Talking like a stranger is itself a sign: the words of those with no real hostility are soon seen through.
edges.quote: are soon seen through

edges.reason: Says how all who love give themselves away, not just this pair.
edges.quote: the words of the loving

couplets.sensitive: reads a rebuff as hidden goodwill, which could excuse ignoring a no

couplets.gloss: A mild telling-off and a cross look are how someone who secretly loves you behaves while acting as if they don't.
couplets.sensitive: reads a rebuff as hidden love, which could excuse ignoring a no

edges.reason: Names small harsh words and cross looks as the signs of those who only act like strangers.
edges.quote: the signs of people who are close but act like strangers

couplets.gloss: When she sees me pleading she softens and gives a small smile, and that smile makes her lovelier still.

edges.reason: Her slow smile when he looks at her brings out a beauty in her.
edges.quote: There is a beauty then in this woman of swaying grace

couplets.gloss: Only people in love can give each other that blank, indifferent look, as though they had never met.

edges.reason: Makes a stranger’s blank look, turned on each other, a mark found only among lovers.
edges.quote: Looking at each other with a blank look, as strangers do

edges.reason: Claims this look for lovers alone, as a thing that belongs to them.
edges.quote: found only among lovers

couplets.gloss: Once two people's eyes have said yes to each other, there's no need for words.

edges.reason: Once eyes have agreed, nothing spoken can add to it.
edges.quote: the words of the mouth are no use at all

couplets.gloss: Everything the five senses can enjoy, I find all together in this one woman.

edges.reason: Finds the full pleasure of all five senses in one woman.
edges.quote: All that the five senses know

couplets.gloss: Normally the cure for an illness is something other than what caused it, but only she can heal the ache she gives me.

edges.reason: Gives desire’s odd rule: the one who causes the sickness is the one who cures it.
edges.quote: she herself is the medicine

edges.reason: Sets this sickness against every other illness, whose cure lies somewhere other than its cause.
edges.quote: The medicine for an illness is something else

couplets.gloss: Could even the heaven of the gods be sweeter than lying in the arms of the person you love?

edges.reason: Asks whether the world of the lotus-eyed one could be sweeter than sleep on soft shoulders.
edges.quote: sleep on the soft shoulders of the one you love

couplets.gloss: She scorches me when she's away and cools me when she's close: what sort of fire behaves like that?

edges.reason: He pictures a fire of hers that burns from far off and cools when close.
edges.quote: It burns when you move away and cools when you come near

couplets.gloss: Whatever I happen to crave at that moment, being with her feels like having exactly that.

edges.reason: Being with her becomes whatever his heart wants at that moment.
edges.quote: like whatever you want, just when you want it

couplets.gloss: Her arms must be made of the food of the gods, because each touch brings me back to life.

edges.reason: Her shoulders are made of the food of immortality, since touching them makes his life put out new leaves.
edges.quote: made of ambrosia

edges.reason: Each touch of hers makes his life put out new leaves.
edges.quote: my life puts out new leaves

couplets.gloss: Holding her gives the same deep satisfaction as eating your own food in your own home after sharing it with others.

edges.reason: Likens her embrace to the contentment of a householder eating at home after giving to others.
edges.quote: like staying in your own home and eating your share of what is yours

couplets.gloss: For two people in love, the best embrace is one so close that not even air can get between them.

edges.reason: Finds the joy in a hold so close that air itself cannot part them.
edges.quote: an embrace that not even the air can cut through

edges.reason: Speaks of what the two who love each other feel together, not of him alone.
edges.quote: two who love each other

couplets.gloss: The sulk, the making up, and then holding each other again: these are the real rewards of being in love.

edges.reason: Counts the sulk itself among the pleasures lovers get.
edges.quote: Sulking, making up and coming together

edges.reason: Making up and coming together are named as what desire pays out.
edges.quote: making up and coming together

edges.reason: Names what every pair of lovers gets from being together.
edges.quote: those who have joined in desire

couplets.gloss: The more you learn, the more you see how little you know, and the closer I get to her, the more there is to love.

edges.reason: Desire grows with each embrace, as learning only uncovers more ignorance.
edges.quote: Desire is like that, each time I hold this woman in red jewels close

couplets.gloss: The anicham is the softest of flowers, yet the woman I love is more delicate than even that.

edges.reason: Tells the softest of flowers that his beloved is tenderer still.
edges.quote: the one I love is softer than you

edges.reason: The aṉiccam, byword for softness, is the standard she passes.
edges.quote: aṉiccam flower

couplets.gloss: My heart, you get flustered at every flower, imagining that blooms anyone can look at could match her eyes.

edges.reason: Flowers everyone can see are too common to be compared with her eye.
edges.quote: blooms that everyone can see

edges.reason: The sight of any flower sets off thoughts of her eyes.
edges.quote: when you see flowers you lose your wits

edges.reason: He scolds his own heart for being fooled by a flower.
edges.quote: My heart

couplets.gloss: Praises her piece by piece: arms like bamboo, skin like a new leaf, pearl teeth, fragrant breath, eyes as sharp as a spear.

edges.reason: Goes over her from shoulder to eye, matching each part to something fine.
edges.quote: her smile is pearl

edges.reason: Gives her eyes the piercing edge of a spear.
edges.quote: her kohl-lined eyes are spears

couplets.gloss: Even the blue water-lily hangs its head when it sees her, knowing it can never be as lovely as her eyes.

edges.reason: The flower itself gives up hope of matching her eye.
edges.quote: We can’t match the eyes of this woman in fine jewels

edges.reason: The blue lily bows its head before her eyes like a beaten rival.
edges.quote: it would bow its head and look at the ground

couplets.gloss: She has worn anicham flowers without trimming the stems, and her waist is so slight that the weight will snap it.

edges.reason: Jokes that her waist is so slight a few flower stems could break it.
edges.quote: No good drums will sound for her waist now

edges.reason: Even the stems of the lightest flower are a load too heavy for her.
edges.quote: aṉiccam flowers without pinching off the stems

couplets.gloss: The stars have lost their way because they can't tell her face from the moon.

edges.reason: Her face throws the very stars into confusion.
edges.quote: the stars have been thrown from their places

edges.reason: Her face is a second moon, so like the first that the stars go astray.
edges.quote: Unable to tell the moon from this woman’s face

couplets.gloss: The moon wanes and fills out again and still carries its mark, but her face has no blemish like that.

edges.reason: Asks whether her face has any mark, expecting the answer no.
edges.quote: Is there a spot on this woman’s face

edges.reason: The moon, with its waning and its spot, is shown up by her unmarked face.
edges.quote: as there is on the bright moon

couplets.gloss: Moon, if you can ever glow like her face, then you will have my love too.

edges.reason: Her face is the standard the moon would have to reach to win him.
edges.quote: If you can shine like this woman’s face

edges.reason: He speaks to the moon as a rival with a chance of earning his love.
edges.quote: you too can have my love

couplets.gloss: Moon, if you want to be like her face, stop showing yourself to everyone and shine only for me.

edges.reason: Her face is what the moon would like to copy, and it is not shown to all the world.
edges.quote: the face of this woman with eyes like flowers

edges.reason: Tells the moon it must give up shining for everyone if it wants to be her equal.
edges.quote: don’t appear for all to see

couplets.gloss: Anicham petals and the softest feathers would feel like prickly burrs under her tender feet.

edges.reason: Her feet are so tender that the softest things would prick them.
edges.quote: to this woman’s feet

edges.reason: Even the aṉiccam, softest of things, would prick her like a thorny fruit.
edges.quote: The aṉiccam flower and the swan’s down

couplets.gloss: The taste of her lips, as she speaks so softly, is like honey stirred into milk.

edges.reason: Tastes the moisture of her mouth as milk and honey mixed together.
edges.quote: like milk mixed with honey

couplets.gloss: The bond between the two of us is as close as the one between body and soul.

edges.reason: Measures his love by the tie that holds soul and body together.
edges.quote: the bond between body and soul

couplets.gloss: Little figure in the pupil of my eye, move out: the woman I love needs that place and nowhere else is good enough for her.

edges.reason: He orders the reflection out of his pupil so that she can live there instead.
edges.quote: the pupil of mine eye

couplets.gloss: With her I feel alive, and when she goes it feels like dying.

edges.reason: Her nearness is life to him and her leaving is death.
edges.quote: when she leaves, she is death to it

couplets.sensitive: Treats a lover’s absence as death.

couplets.gloss: I could only call her virtues to mind if I had first forgotten them, and I have no idea how to forget them.

edges.reason: He cannot even recall her, since recalling would need a moment of having forgotten.
edges.quote: I don’t know how to forget

couplets.gloss: He never leaves my eyes and blinking doesn't hurt him, because my love is too fine a thing to be harmed.

edges.reason: She keeps him seated in her eye, where even a blink cannot bruise him.
edges.quote: He will not go from my eyes

couplets.gloss: He lives inside my eyes, so I won't even put on eyeliner in case I lose sight of him for a moment.

edges.reason: Her eye is his home, so she gives up painting it rather than blink him away.
edges.quote: My beloved dwelleth ever within my eyes

couplets.gloss: He lives in my heart, so I stay away from hot food in case it burns him.
I don't blink in case I miss him for even a moment, and because of this the villagers call him heartless.

edges.reason: The town takes her unblinking devotion as proof that he is a stranger to her.
edges.quote: this town calls him a stranger

couplets.gloss: He happily lives in my heart and never leaves it, yet the neighbours say he has deserted me and call him cruel.

edges.reason: They say he has left her, not knowing he has never left her heart.
edges.quote: This town says he lives apart from me

couplets.gloss: For someone cut off from the one they love and suffering badly, the only option left is the public ordeal of riding the palm stem.
couplets.sensitive: treats a self-wounding public ordeal as love’s only way out

edges.reason: Holds up the palmyra stalk as the one refuge left to those who ache with desire.
edges.quote: no refuge and no strength but the palmyra stalk

edges.reason: Speaks for all who ache with desire, not for himself alone.
edges.quote: those who suffer and ache with desire

couplets.gloss: Unable to take the pain any longer, my body and soul have agreed to the public ride and thrown all shame aside.
couplets.sensitive: resolves on the self-wounding ride because the pain cannot be borne

edges.reason: Body and soul agree to the ride because they can bear the pain no longer.
edges.quote: will ride the palmyra stalk

couplets.gloss: I used to have self-respect and modesty, but all I have now is the stem that desperate lovers ride.
keywords: love made a fool of me
couplets.sensitive: the self-wounding ride is all he says he has left

edges.reason: The stalk is now what he has, in place of the shame and manly strength he once had.
edges.quote: Today I have the palmyra stalk

couplets.gloss: I relied on my self-control and modesty to keep me afloat, but the flood of desire swept all that away.

edges.reason: Shame and manly strength were the raft he trusted, and it went with the flood.
edges.quote: the raft of shame and good manly strength

couplets.gloss: This delicate girl with her small bangles is the one who has left me with that desperate ride and the misery of every evening.
couplets.sensitive: names the self-wounding ride as what she has left him with

edges.reason: He lays the stalk at her door, as something she herself has handed him.
edges.quote: gave me the palmyra stalk

edges.reason: Dusk is the second thing she gave him, a grief of its own.
edges.quote: the sorrow that comes with the evening

couplets.gloss: I can't sleep for thinking about her, so I will make that desperate ride tonight, late as it is.
couplets.sensitive: a sleepless lover resolves on the self-wounding ride

edges.reason: Sleeplessness keeps his mind on riding the stalk.
edges.quote: I think of riding the palmyra stalk

edges.reason: Midnight finds him awake, thinking of the ride.
edges.quote: Even at midnight

couplets.gloss: Nothing is finer than a woman who, however overwhelmed by love, keeps it in and never makes that desperate public ride.
couplets.sensitive: praises a woman for bearing love’s pain in silence; the ride it names is self-wounding

edges.reason: Rates nothing above the woman who bears desire without the ride, however vast it is.
edges.quote: Nothing is greater than a woman

edges.reason: The stalk is the step she refuses, whatever desire puts her through.
edges.quote: still doesn’t ride the palmyra stalk

edges.reason: Her desire is measured by the vastness of the sea.
edges.quote: desire as vast as the sea

couplets.gloss: My love takes no account of my self-restraint or how gently I've treated it: it breaks cover and shows itself in public.

edges.reason: Desire heeds neither firmness nor pity, and breaks out of its own hiding.
edges.quote: It breaks out of hiding into the open

couplets.gloss: Thinking nobody has noticed it, my love roams through the streets in a daze of distress.
Thoughtless people laugh at me openly because they have never gone through what I am going through.

edges.reason: Those who jeer at her are the onlookers of her love, wrong because they have felt none of it.
edges.quote: Fools laugh in front of my eyes

couplets.gloss: The village gossip about us keeps me alive, and luckily most people don't realise that.

edges.reason: The talk that ought to shame him gives him back his life.
edges.quote: As the outcry riseth in the village my life cometh back to me

couplets.gloss: The villagers have no idea how rare she is, or they wouldn't have handed her to me so cheaply through their talk.

edges.reason: Their ignorance of her worth is what lets them pair her with him so lightly.
edges.quote: this town has made me a gift of gossip

edges.reason: Their talk hands her to him at a price far below her worth.
edges.quote: they have given her cheaply to me by raising this clamour

couplets.gloss: The talk around the village is a gift to me, because it makes me feel she is mine even though she isn't.

edges.reason: Village talk lets him feel he already has her, though he has not won her.
edges.quote: It feels as if I have what I haven’t got

couplets.gloss: All the talk has made me want her more; without it this would have gone flat.

edges.reason: The gossip is what keeps his desire from shrinking away.
edges.quote: Gossip is what makes my desire grow

couplets.gloss: Just as each drink makes a drinker want another, each time others find out about a man's love it tastes sweeter to him.

edges.reason: Coming into the open works on desire as getting drunk works on the thirst for toddy.
edges.quote: getting drunk makes you want more toddy

edges.reason: Every time others find out, the love only tastes sweeter.
edges.quote: every discovery of his passion by others

edges.reason: Turns from his own case to say what exposure does for any lover.
edges.quote: its sweetness for the lover

couplets.gloss: We met just once, yet the uproar is as huge as an eclipse, when everyone runs outside to look.

edges.reason: One day's meeting raises a noise far out of scale with it.
edges.quote: the outcry that hath arisen over it

edges.reason: The eclipse is a snake seizing the moon, news that spreads through the whole world.
edges.quote: the snake seizing the moon

edges.reason: The swallowed moon sets the scale of the village's excitement.
edges.quote: swallowed the moon

couplets.gloss: The neighbours' talk fertilises this love-sickness and my mother's scolding waters it, so between them it keeps on growing.

edges.reason: Talk and a mother’s harsh words are manure and water, feeding the very thing they oppose.
edges.quote: The town’s gossip is the manure

edges.reason: Anyone under pressure from neighbours and family can see that such talk feeds a love rather than ends it.
edges.quote: this sickness grows on

edges.reason: Gossip and a mother’s scolding only feed the pain, as manure and water feed a plant.
edges.quote: The town’s gossip is the manure and my mother’s words the water

couplets.gloss: Trying to kill my love with scandal is like trying to put out a fire by pouring on butter.

edges.reason: Scandal cannot put a love out, any more than ghee can put out a blaze.
edges.quote: To think of extinguishing my passion by raising this clamour

edges.reason: Desire is a flame, and the gossip is ghee poured on it.
edges.quote: put out a fire with ghee

edges.reason: Tells anyone being shamed out of a love that the shaming will only feed it.
edges.quote: To say you will put out desire with gossip

couplets.gloss: Why should I be embarrassed by the talk now, when the man who told me not to worry has left me exposed to everyone?
The villagers have raised the very talk I was hoping for, and now if I ask him, my love will surely grant what I want.

edges.reason: The town has unwittingly done them a favour with its gossip.
edges.quote: This town is raising the gossip we wanted

edges.reason: Far from dreading the talk, she has been wishing for it.
edges.quote: This clamour which I in my heart so much desire

couplets.gloss: If you're staying, tell me; if all you have is a promise to hurry back, save it for someone who'll still be alive when you do.
couplets.sensitive: says she will not survive his leaving

edges.reason: Even the promise of a quick return is refused, because she will not live to see it.
edges.quote: tell that to whoever will still be alive

edges.reason: Spoken straight to the man about to leave her.
edges.quote: If you aren’t going, tell me

couplets.gloss: Just seeing him used to make me happy, but now even when he holds me I'm sad, because I'm afraid he's going to leave.

edges.reason: Fear of his going sours even the embrace that would once have been pure joy.
edges.quote: our union itself holds the pain of fearing he will leave

couplets.gloss: How can I trust anyone, when even the person who understands me best has leaving somewhere in his mind?

edges.reason: If even the one who knows her heart can think of leaving, she sees no one left to trust.
edges.quote: Even those who understand can sometimes leave

couplets.gloss: He told me not to be afraid; if he now agrees to leave, how can it be my fault that I believed his promise?
If you want to keep me alive, stop him leaving, because once he goes I doubt we will ever be together again.
couplets.sensitive: treats his going as the end of her life

edges.reason: She turns to her maid as the one person who might yet stop him.
edges.quote: If you would save me

edges.reason: Before he has even gone she has given up hope of their meeting again.
edges.quote: it will be hard to meet again

couplets.gloss: If he can be cold enough to tell me to my face that he's leaving, I can't hope he will ever come back and be kind to me.

edges.reason: The bare words of leaving are enough to end her hope.
edges.quote: there is little hope that he will be kind

couplets.gloss: My bangles, once tight, now slide off my wrists, and they will tell everyone that he has left me.

edges.reason: Her slipping bangles will spread the word of the parting.
edges.quote: these bangles slipping from my forearm

couplets.gloss: Living somewhere without close friends is hard, but being separated from the one you love is harder still.

edges.reason: Ranks being parted from the beloved as bitterer than living friendless.
edges.quote: More painful still is parting from those dear to you

couplets.gloss: Fire only burns you if you touch it; can it burn from a distance the way love does?

edges.reason: Fire is the lesser burner, needing touch where desire burns from far off.
edges.quote: Fire burns if you touch it

edges.reason: Says what sets desire apart: it burns when you are away from it.
edges.quote: burn when you leave it, as the sickness of desire does

couplets.gloss: So many people, apparently, bear the pain of goodbye and separation and live to see their partner return. I can't imagine how.

edges.reason: Marvels that anyone can bear the parting and go on living afterwards.
edges.quote: bear the parting and go on living afterwards

couplets.gloss: I try to keep this pain hidden, but the more I push it down the more it rises, like a spring when you bail it out.

edges.reason: Hiding the sickness only raises it, as drawing from a spring brings up more water.
edges.quote: it rises like spring water

couplets.gloss: I can't hide this pain any more, yet I'd be too ashamed to tell it even to the man who caused it.
keywords: can't tell him how i feel

edges.reason: The grief has grown past the point where she can keep it hidden.
edges.quote: I can’t hide this sickness

edges.reason: Shame stops her telling even the man who caused the pain.
edges.quote: telling the one who caused it brings me shame

couplets.gloss: Love and modesty hang like two heavy loads from my life as if from a carrying pole, and my worn-out body can't take it.

edges.reason: One of the two loads hung from the pole of her life.
edges.quote: Desire and shame hang from my life

edges.reason: The load at the other end, weighing as heavily as her desire.
edges.quote: Desire and shame hang from my life

couplets.sensitive: Pictures the body breaking under grief.

couplets.gloss: My love is a whole ocean in front of me, and I have no boat that could get me across.

edges.reason: Her desire lies before her as a sea to be crossed.
edges.quote: a sea of desire

edges.reason: No safe raft exists to carry her over it.
edges.quote: no safe raft to cross it

couplets.gloss: If he lets me waste away like this while he's supposed to love me, what would he do if he were my enemy?
keywords: hurt by someone who loves you

couplets.gloss: Love brings joy as big as the ocean, but when it turns painful the suffering is even bigger.

edges.reason: Gives desire its two measures: joy as wide as the sea, and pain greater still.
edges.quote: The joy of desire is a sea

edges.reason: The sea is the measure of desire’s joy, and its pain goes past even that.
edges.quote: the pain is greater than that sea

couplets.gloss: I'm swimming through a raging flood of love and can't see land, and deep in the night I'm the only one awake.

edges.reason: Alone in the dark with no shore in view: a grief with no end and no comfort.
edges.quote: see no shore

edges.reason: She swims the fierce flood of desire with no shore in sight.
edges.quote: I swim the fierce flood of desire

edges.reason: The dead of night is when her aloneness is complete.
edges.quote: Even at midnight I alone am here

couplets.gloss: Night kindly puts every living thing to sleep, and I'm the only one left awake to keep her company.

edges.reason: Night puts all the world to sleep and leaves her as its one companion.
edges.quote: has no companion but me

couplets.gloss: These long nights that drag on are even crueller to me than the cruel man who left me.

edges.reason: In her wakeful grief the slow hours hurt more than his desertion.
edges.quote: Crueller even than that cruel one’s cruelty

edges.reason: Night is given a cruelty of its own, outdoing his.
edges.quote: these nights that now drag on

couplets.gloss: If my eyes could go to him the way my heart does, they wouldn't be drowning in tears right now.

edges.reason: Her tears have become a flood that her eyes must swim.
edges.quote: swimming in this flood of water

edges.reason: Her eyes are pictured as unable to follow where her heart goes.
edges.quote: If my eyes could go where he is, as my heart does

couplets.gloss: Why are my eyes crying to me now, when they're the ones who showed him to me and brought on this endless sorrow?
keywords: if only i hadn't seen him

edges.reason: She faces her eyes, who weep though they brought the sickness on by showing him to her.
edges.quote: Why do my eyes weep now?

couplets.gloss: My eyes looked at him without thinking that day, so why do they grieve now instead of putting up with what they did?

edges.reason: Blames her eyes for one rash look and asks why they suffer now.
edges.quote: These kohl-lined eyes looked without knowing what would come

couplets.gloss: They rushed to look at him by their own choice and now they cry by their own choice: what a joke they are.

edges.reason: Mocks her eyes, which chose to look and now choose to weep.
edges.quote: There is something laughable in this

couplets.gloss: My eyes left me with this pain that can't be cured, and now they have cried themselves dry.

edges.reason: Her eyes left the sickness fixed in her, then ran dry.
edges.quote: they can’t weep, their water gone

edges.reason: The store of tears is spent while the grief stays on.
edges.quote: having exhausted their store of tears

couplets.gloss: My eyes gave me pain bigger than the ocean, and now they suffer too and can't even sleep.

edges.reason: The eyes that caused her sickness are themselves now suffering and sleepless.
edges.quote: now suffer and can’t close

edges.reason: What her eyes brought on is wider than the sea.
edges.quote: too great for the sea

couplets.gloss: It's a satisfying kind of payback that the eyes that brought on my misery are now suffering the very same thing.

edges.reason: Treats her own eyes as a foe and relishes seeing them suffer as she does.
edges.quote: have fallen into it themselves

couplets.gloss: Those eyes stared at him so hungrily that day; let them weep on and on until there is nothing left in them.
couplets.sensitive: wishes her own eyes wasted away as a punishment

edges.reason: She curses her eyes for their longing gaze and wishes them dry.
edges.quote: Let them suffer and suffer till their water runs out

couplets.gloss: So there are people who love without being loved in return: look at my eyes, which can't rest unless they see him.

edges.reason: States the fact of it: he wanted her without cherishing her, and still her eyes want him.
edges.quote: There is one who wanted me without cherishing me

edges.reason: Her restless eyes are her proof that one can love unloved.
edges.quote: my eyes will not rest until they see him

couplets.gloss: My eyes can't sleep when he's gone and can't sleep when he's back, so they're in pain either way.

edges.reason: Absent or home, he keeps her eyes awake and hurting.
edges.quote: When he doesn’t come they don’t sleep

couplets.gloss: When your own eyes announce everything like a drum, as mine do, outsiders have no trouble working out your secret.

edges.reason: Eyes are drums that beat out the secret they are meant to keep.
edges.quote: whose eyes are beaten drums

edges.reason: The townsfolk read her secret straight off her eyes.
edges.quote: It isn’t hard for the town to find out the secret

couplets.gloss: I'm the one who agreed to let him go, so who can I complain to now that I've turned pale?

edges.reason: She has no one to tell of her paleness, having consented to the parting herself.
edges.quote: Who can I tell now that I have turned pale

couplets.gloss: This paleness is proud to be his offspring, and it creeps all over my body as if I were its mount.

edges.reason: Pallor is cast as his child, riding proudly over her body.
edges.quote: pallor climbs on my body and rides it

couplets.gloss: He took my looks and my modesty and gave me only heartache and a sickly colour in return.

edges.reason: Her pale colour is part of what he paid her with, in exchange for her looks.
edges.quote: gave me sickness and pallor

couplets.gloss: I think only of him and speak only in his praise, yet somehow this paleness has spread over me anyway.

edges.reason: Thinking and speaking of him should have kept the pallor off, so she calls it a fraud.
edges.quote: is this pallor a fraud

couplets.gloss: He had only just gone over there, and already the paleness had found me here.

edges.reason: Paleness tracks her down at once, however short a way he has gone.
edges.quote: pallor spreading over my body

couplets.gloss: Paleness waits for him to let go of me, exactly as the dark waits for a lamp to go out.

edges.reason: Pallor waits like an enemy for any break in their closeness.
edges.quote: pallor waits for my husband’s embrace to slacken

edges.reason: His embrace is the lamp that alone keeps the pallor back.
edges.quote: a lamp to fail

edges.reason: Darkness waiting for a light to fail pictures how pallor watches her.
edges.quote: As darkness waits for a lamp to fail

couplets.gloss: I was lying in his arms, shifted away for a moment, and the paleness swallowed me whole.
keywords: can't be apart for a second

edges.reason: A moment’s shift out of his arms is enough for pallor to engulf her.
edges.quote: pallor came on so thick you could scoop it up

couplets.gloss: People find fault with me for looking pale and thin, but nobody finds fault with him for leaving me.

edges.reason: Her pale skin draws the blame, while his desertion goes unremarked.
edges.quote: She has turned pale

edges.reason: The reproachful people are the neighbours, wrong as ever about where the fault lies.
edges.quote: No one says, “He has left her.”

couplets.gloss: Let my body go deathly pale, as long as the man who won my love comes out of this well.
couplets.sensitive: accepts wasting away so long as the man who hurt her is cleared of blame

edges.reason: Her pale body is the price set against his being cleared.
edges.quote: Let my body turn as pale as it will

edges.reason: She turns on the maid who would clear him of blame.
edges.quote: my maid

couplets.gloss: Better that people mock me for how pale I've become, as long as they don't call my partner cruel.
couplets.sensitive: accepts ridicule to shield a partner from being called cruel

edges.reason: She will take the jibes about her colour to keep the blame off him.
edges.quote: It is well to be called pallor itself

couplets.gloss: Only people loved back by the person they love get to enjoy love's sweet fruit, with no hard stone in it.

edges.reason: Desire tastes wholly sweet only to those whose love is returned.
edges.quote: Those whose love is returned by the one they love

edges.reason: Returned love is a fruit with no stone to bite on.
edges.quote: the stoneless fruit of desire

couplets.gloss: The kindness of the one you love is to you what rain is to everything that lives.

edges.reason: A lover’s kindness sustains the one who loves, as rain sustains those who live by it.
edges.quote: like rain from the sky to those who live by it

couplets.gloss: Only people whose love is returned have any right to call themselves happy.

edges.reason: Keeps the pride of happiness for those loved in return.
edges.quote: Only those loved by the ones they love can have the pride

edges.reason: Reserving happiness for returned love marks out what the unreturned kind lacks.
edges.quote: who are loved in return by those whom they love

couplets.gloss: Being admired by other people means nothing: if a woman isn't loved by the one she loves, she has no happiness.
keywords: loved by others but not by him
couplets.sensitive: tells an unloved woman she can have no happiness at all

edges.reason: Being held dear by others counts for nothing beside the one love she lacks.
edges.quote: if the one they love doesn’t love them back

couplets.gloss: What can I expect from the person I love if he doesn't love me the way I love him?

edges.reason: Hope of any kindness dies when love runs only one way.
edges.quote: if he doesn’t love me too

edges.reason: Puts the hard question to anyone hoping for something from a person who does not love back.
edges.quote: What can the one I love do for me

couplets.gloss: Love is like a load on a shoulder pole: easy when balanced at both ends, miserable when it hangs from only one.

edges.reason: Gives the figure of it: a load hung from one end of the pole alone.
edges.quote: Desire on one side only is painful

edges.reason: Tells anyone carrying a love alone why it weighs so much: it is only light when shared.
edges.quote: it is sweet when it is on both sides

couplets.gloss: Love's god attacks only me and leaves him alone: can't he see how much I'm suffering?

edges.reason: The god of desire stays on one side only, leaving her to suffer alone.
edges.quote: stays on one side only

couplets.gloss: Nobody is harder than a woman who carries on living without one kind word from the man she loves.
couplets.sensitive: calls women who go on living without his love hard-hearted, implying they should not

couplets.gloss: Even if the one I long for is unkind to me, any word of him is lovely to hear.
couplets.sensitive: finds any word from an unkind partner sweet, which could hold someone in a harmful bond

edges.reason: Even with unkindness in return, a bare word from him stays sweet.
edges.quote: any word of him is sweet to my ears

couplets.gloss: Good luck, my heart: telling your pain to someone who doesn't love you is like trying to empty the ocean.
keywords: talking to someone who doesn't care

edges.reason: She gives her heart a mocking blessing on its useless errand.
edges.quote: Long may you live, my heart

edges.reason: Filling in the sea would be easier than this telling.
edges.quote: Fill in the sea instead

edges.reason: Tells anyone pleading with a person who does not love them that the effort is futile.
edges.quote: You would tell your sickness to one who isn’t close to you

couplets.gloss: Just remembering love brings joy that never runs out, which makes love better than any drink.
keywords: thinking of you makes me happy

edges.reason: Mere remembering gives a joy that doesn’t fade.
edges.quote: even thinking of it brings a great joy that doesn’t fade

edges.reason: Toddy loses to desire, which delights even when only remembered.
edges.quote: Desire is sweeter than toddy

couplets.gloss: As soon as I picture the one I love, all my sadness lifts: love is lovely in every way.
keywords: thinking of someone cheers me up

edges.reason: Thinking of the one you love keeps all pain away.
edges.quote: When you think of the one you love, no pain comes

edges.reason: Offers someone apart from a partner a comfort they can reach for at will: bring them to mind.
edges.quote: When you think of the one you love

couplets.gloss: I nearly sneezed but it went away: did he start to think of me and then stop?

edges.reason: A sneeze that fades becomes proof of a thought of her that he let drop.
edges.quote: A sneeze starts to come and then dies away

couplets.gloss: Do I have any place in his heart at all? He certainly never leaves mine.
keywords: does he still think of me

edges.reason: Sure of her own heart, she doubts her place in his, which is the test of this love.
edges.quote: Am I too in his heart?

couplets.gloss: He keeps me shut out of his heart, so how can he not be ashamed to keep turning up in mine all the time?

edges.reason: He bars her from his heart yet never leaves hers.
edges.quote: He has barred me from his heart

couplets.gloss: Only the memory of the days we spent together keeps me going; what other life do I have?

edges.reason: Memory of their union is all that still holds her in life.
edges.quote: I live by remembering the days I was with him

couplets.sensitive: Ties staying alive to an absent lover.

couplets.gloss: Even with him always in my thoughts my heart is on fire; what would become of me if I forgot him?

edges.reason: Memory scorches her, yet she fears forgetting more.
edges.quote: What would become of me if I forgot?

edges.reason: Remembering is a burning inside the heart.
edges.quote: even remembering burns my heart

couplets.gloss: However often I think of him he never gets cross with me for it: that's how good he is to me.
keywords: thinking of him all the time

edges.reason: That he never minds being thought of, however often, is the kindness she credits him with.
edges.quote: However much I think of him, he doesn’t get angry

couplets.gloss: He once said the two of us were one being; when I think how unkind he has been since, I feel the life drain out of me.
couplets.sensitive: speaks of her life ebbing away over his cruelty

edges.reason: His old claim that they shared one soul is what makes his cruelty so deadly.
edges.quote: We are not two but only one life and soul

couplets.gloss: Moon, please don't set until my eyes can see again the man who left me but has never left my heart.

edges.reason: She begs the moon to stay up so that she may yet see him.
edges.quote: O Moon! set not in the horizon

edges.reason: Her one wish is to lay eyes on him again, though he has never left her heart.
edges.quote: so that my eyes may see the one who left without leaving me

ideaLinks.reason: Each time he holds her close his desire grows, as learning only deepens the sense of ignorance.
ideaLinks.quote: Desire is like that, each time I hold this woman in red jewels close

ideaLinks.reason: The flood of desire sweeps away the shame and strength he trusted, and in K1138 it breaks through her hiding too.
ideaLinks.quote: The fierce flood of desire carries off the raft

ideaLinks.reason: Far from ending desire, the gossip is said outright to make it grow.
ideaLinks.quote: Gossip is what makes my desire grow

ideaLinks.reason: Fear of his going takes the delight out of the embrace itself.
ideaLinks.quote: our union itself holds the pain of fearing he will leave

ideaLinks.reason: Says in plain words that desire brings joy, and joy as wide as the sea.
ideaLinks.quote: The joy of desire is a sea

ideaLinks.reason: The desire that gives that joy, once it turns on you, brings pain greater than the joy.
ideaLinks.quote: when it turns on you, the pain is greater than that sea

ideaLinks.reason: Thinking of the absent one keeps the pain of parting away.

proposals.label: The Watered Plant
proposals.why: Love as a young plant fed by water and manure is the whole figure of 1093 and 1147, and of 1304 outside this shard. image:seed-and-sowing covers sowing and crop, not tending a growing plant.

proposals.label: The Carrying Pole
proposals.why: A shoulder pole with a load at each end is the whole figure of 1163 and 1196, and Aiyar stops to explain it. quality:one-sided-love mentions it, but no image entry holds it.
